title: Progressive column stabilizer and density lens for mixed-content virtual grids
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our virtualized table currently jitters and reflows when rows contain mixed-height content (avatars + multi-line descriptions + code blocks). This causes column-resize handles to jump, and density toggles to produce unexpected layout shifts. Goals: (1) reduce perceived jitter during scroll/resize, (2) provide a compact yet discoverable density preview that lets people see the effect before applying a density change, (3) make column-resize affordances tactile and keyboard-accessible while maintaining virtualization performance budgets. Proposed solution: introduce a progressive column stabilizer that pins measured column widths during small viewport/virtualization deltas, plus a density "lens" UI adjacent to the header that shows a hover preview (live snapshot) of the same viewport at alternate densities (compact / default / comfortable). The stabilizer uses a short-lived heuristic window (50–200ms) to avoid reflow thrash while keeping KV cache-friendly virtualization. The density lens is a lightweight overlay canvas that renders a DPI-scaled preview of visible rows (client-side snapshot) and animates to the applied state on commit. Accessibility: keyboard focus on the header toggles a density preview mode; aria-live announcements indicate pending density changes and final applied state. Metrics: target 20–40% reduction in visible header jitter on mixed-content workloads; no more than 5% token-cost-equivalent increase from additional preview render work when enabled.
acceptance_criteria: Column handles remain visually stable during scroll and small layout updates on pages with variable row heights
Density lens preview renders within 80ms of hover on desktop and 200ms on mobile-simulated viewports
Keyboard-only flow: focus + Alt+D opens density lens, arrow keys change density, Enter applies; screen reader announces changes clearly
No regression in continuous-batching latency budgets for hosted integration tests (benchmark suite: table-scroll-1k-mixed) beyond 5%
Design tokens used for density mappings (compact/comfortable/default) and exposed in the tokens spec
engineering_notes: Spike showed stabilizer window 75ms to be a good starting point; can be tuned via dataset histogram
Implement stabilizer outside main render loop where possible (requestIdleCallback fallback) to avoid blocking frames
Density lens should render using an offscreen canvas or virtualized snapshot to avoid DOM repaint costs
We need a feature flag for the density lens to roll out progressively and A/B test client CPU cost
PR template: reference benchmark run IDs and attach flamegraphs for any changes

decisions: Use a short-lived stabilizer (initial 75ms) rather than permanent pinning to avoid long-term layout drift
Density lens implemented as an offscreen canvas preview rather than full DOM clone to minimize repainting
Feature gated behind 'densityLens' flag for controlled rollout and telemetry
